headline: High risk of shared-workspace prompt injection and data leakage; Roo Code can also drive destructive actions while LangGraph orchestrates state across shared checkpointer state.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LangGraph can pass state between nodes and instances via a shared checkpointer store, while Roo Code reads and writes VS Code workspace files and can use MCP. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if one agent consumes the other's file or tool output as trusted text. The pathway is not proven by docs alone, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF LangGraph writes attacker-controlled text into shared state or files that Roo Code later parses as instructions
IF Roo Code exposes file contents or MCP output back into LangGraph without provenance checks
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to every cross-agent message
Restrict shared files to data-only formats
Disable MCP for the shared workflow
Review any file-derived prompts before execution
requires-engineering: add schema validation on inter-agent messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents can read and write filesystem content, and LangGraph explicitly shares state via a checkpointer store while Roo Code shares state via the filesystem. If sensitive workspace data enters that shared surface, either agent can surface it in outputs or send it to model providers. The profiles do not prove PHI or secrets are present, so medium fits.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in the shared workspace or checkpointer store
IF either agent forwards file contents into a model-provider call
mitigations: Move secrets out of the shared workspace
Use separate workspaces per agent
Redact sensitive files before handoff
Limit model-provider access to approved paths
requires-engineering: encrypt or isolate the checkpointer store

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write, shell execution, and broad network egress; Roo Code also modifies git state and installs packages. In a shared workspace, concurrent writes and git mutations can collide and corrupt state or commits. LangGraph's shared checkpointer plus Roo Code's filesystem sharing make the conflict pathway default-dangerous enough for high.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or repository
IF either agent writes while the other is reading or committing
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Serialize write operations with a lock
Pause one agent during git commits
Disable package installs in shared runs
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: LangGraph is an orchestration framework that can emit stateful outputs, and Roo Code can act on workspace content with shell, browser, and git capabilities. If Roo Code treats LangGraph output as authoritative, errors can cascade into destructive edits or external actions. Because the pair can default into action-taking without a built-in verification boundary, high is warranted.
conditions: IF Roo Code consumes LangGraph-produced text as instructions or facts
IF Roo Code executes shell or git actions based on unverified LangGraph output
mitigations: Require human review before actions
Insert a verification step between agents
Mark LangGraph output as untrusted by default
Limit Roo Code to read-only mode for handoffs
requires-engineering: add output attestation and checksums

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and only mention model-provider API keys plus workspace/source-code data, so no specific residency or regulated-data mismatch is evidenced. The main compliance concern is generic logging or retention, but the profiles do not show a concrete policy conflict. I do not cite only one agent because the pairwise compliance question needs both profiles to rule out a mismatch.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into the shared workspace
IF one deployment enforces retention or residency rules that the other does not
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Document retention settings for both tools
Use separate storage regions
Review logging defaults before deployment
requires-engineering: align compliance controls across both agents
